stem.en: Strong earthquakes from 2000 to 2024 are plotted on a world map. Where do most of them fall?

text.en: On lines of latitude, mostly the equator

feedback.en: No. The belts cross many latitudes.

text.en: Along every coast of every continent

feedback.en: No. Many coasts have few strong earthquakes, such as eastern South America.

text.en: In long belts, mainly round the Pacific

feedback.en: Yes. The largest belt is the Ring of Fire.

text.en: Evenly over all of the land and sea

feedback.en: No. Wide areas have almost none.

explanation.en: Strong earthquakes fall along long, narrow belts. The largest is the Ring of Fire around the Pacific Ocean. A second runs from the Mediterranean through the Himalaya, and a thin line follows the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

hints.en: Are the dots spread out or lined up?
Which ocean has a belt all the way round it?
